subtitle: Ledgers of the Lion: How Numbers Held Up the Eastern Ganga Realm

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close-up of a bearded Eastern Ganga Mint Master holding a gleaming gold fanam, Konark Sun Temple looming ghostlike behind him
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master stands in a dim mint hall, palm raised with a tiny gold fanam catching a shaft of sunlight, while in the distant haze the silhouette of the Konark Sun Temple rises like a stone chariot.

dialogue.text: Temples of stone, armies of steel: yet the Eastern Ganga kingdom stood on copper plates, Anka years and gold fanams marked by tiny decimal signs of power.

i18n.hi: पत्थर के मंदिर, लोहे की सेनाएँ – पर पूर्वी गंगा राज्य टिकता था तांबे की पट्टियों पर, अंक वर्षों पर और छोटे दशमलवी निशान वाले सोने के फनमों पर।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a table strewn with copper plates, palm-leaf manuscripts and coins beside a map of Eastern Ganga Orissa
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master leans over a wooden table, one hand on a rolled map of Orissa, the other near neatly arranged copper plate grants and small gold fanams, with palm-leaf manuscripts stacked beside him.

dialogue.text: Between the 11th and 14th centuries, the Eastern Ganga rulers in Cuttack and Puri needed more than devotion and war. They needed a working machine of land, records and coin.

i18n.hi: ११वीं से १४वीं सदी के बीच, कटक और पुरी के पूर्वी गंगा शासकों को सिर्फ भक्ति और युद्ध नहीं, ज़मीन, रजिस्टर और सिक्कों की चालू मशीन चाहिए थी।

panels.shot: wide top-down view over a schematic landscape showing mahamandala, mandala, vishaya and villages connected like a web
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master’s hand hovers above a drawn parchment where hills, rivers and towns are labeled, lines linking large circles as mahamandala, mid circles as mandala, smaller dots as vishaya and clusters of tiny huts as villages.

dialogue.text: Copper plates like the Sindurapura grant list a clear ladder of rule: mahamandala at the top, then mandala, then vishaya, down to the village where the tax was actually paid.

i18n.hi: सिंदुरापुरा ताम्रपट जैसी दानपत्रों में राज की सीढ़ी साफ दिखती है – ऊपर महामंडल, फिर मंडल, फिर विशय, नीचे वही गाँव जहाँ से कर वसूला जाता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of village officials standing before a local shrine while a scribe writes on palm leaf
panels.action: In a rural setting under a banyan tree, village elders and officials stand near a small shrine, while Eastern Ganga Mint Master, dressed as a Karan scribe, sits on the ground inscribing a palm-leaf manuscript with a stylus.

dialogue.text: At the bottom stood the village officers and the Karans, the record-keepers. They fixed boundaries, listed fields, and turned spoken promises into written grants.

i18n.hi: सबसे नीचे गाँव के अफसर और करन लेखक खड़े थे। वे सीमा तय करते, खेत गिनते और ज़बानी वादों को लिखित दान में बदल देते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of the scribe’s hand incising Odia script onto a copper plate
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master carefully engraves lines of early Odia script on a glowing copper plate held firm by pegs, his face intent in the lamplight of a royal office.

dialogue.text: When a king gave land, the Karan’s script cut it into copper. The Sindurapura grant and others name officers, villages and shares with careful detail from top to bottom.

i18n.hi: जब राजा ज़मीन देता, करन की लिपि उसे तांबे पर काट देती। sindurapura ताम्रपट और दूसरे दान ऊपर से नीचे तक अफसरों, गाँवों और हिस्सों को बारीकी से गिनाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside Cuttack royal office, officers reporting to a seated administrator with heaps of records
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master sits as a senior administrator in Cuttack, backed by shelves of palm leaves and plates, while subordinate officers from different mandalas stand before him with rolled documents and ledger bundles.

dialogue.text: Panigrahi and Sahu show an ordered hierarchy: local units reported upwards, building a regional state. Information flowed to Cuttack and Puri like rivers to the sea.

i18n.hi: पाणिग्राही और साहू एक सजी हुई पदानुक्रम दिखाते हैं – छोटे इकाई ऊपर रिपोर्ट करते, और मिलकर क्षेत्रीय राज्य बनाते। जानकारी कटक और पुरी में ऐसे बहती जैसे नदियाँ समुंदर में।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a palm-leaf roll labeled as temple chronicle being placed in a chest
panels.action: In a chamber near a temple model, Eastern Ganga Mint Master gently rolls a palm-leaf manuscript and places it into a wooden chest filled with similar rolls, priests visible in the background.

dialogue.text: Alongside royal ledgers grew temple chronicles. The Madala Panji tradition of Puri would later remember kings, grants and rituals, though its exact early form is debated by historians.

i18n.hi: राजकीय बहीखातों के साथ-साथ मंदिर की पुराणियाँ भी उगती गईं। पुरी की मडला पंजी परंपरा बाद में राजाओं, दान और अनुष्ठान याद रखेगी, भले उसके शुरुआती रूप पर इतिहासकारों में मतभेद हो।

panels.shot: dramatic side shot of the Mint Master watching molten metal being poured into coin molds
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master stands in a smoky mint hall, watching workers pour molten gold into small molds, their faces lit by the furnace glow and rows of tiny fanam blanks cooling on a stone slab.

dialogue.text: Records alone could not move armies or pay builders. For that, the Eastern Ganga rulers struck gold fanams—tiny coins of high value, born from flame and weighed with care.

i18n.hi: रिकॉर्ड अकेले सेनाएँ नहीं चलाते, न ही राजमिस्त्री की मज़दूरी भरते। इसके लिए पूर्वी गंगा राजाओं ने सोने के फनम गढ़े – छोटे पर कीमती सिक्के, आग में जन्मे, तराज़ू पर परखे गए।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a coin die about to strike a fanam, showing lion and legend side
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master positions a coin die above a small gold blank on an anvil, the carved lion and legend side of the die visible, as his hammer is raised mid-air.

dialogue.text: On one face, the fanam carried royal signs—often a lion or sacred emblems, naming the Eastern Ganga authority. This side spoke of kingship and divine claim.

i18n.hi: एक तरफ फनम पर राजचिह्न थे – अक्सर सिंह या पवित्र निशान, जो पूर्वी गंगा सत्ता का नाम लिखते। यही साइड राजत्व और दैवी हक की भाषा बोलती थी।

panels.shot: macro shot of the reverse of a struck fanam showing tiny numerals in positional alignment
panels.action: Under a beam of light, Eastern Ganga Mint Master holds a finished fanam with tweezers, its reverse showing minute numerals aligned in a row, while other coins lie scattered like golden seeds.

dialogue.text: On the reverse, A.K. Singh notes, some fanams show numerals set in places—a clear use of decimal positional notation, among the earliest well-attested Hindu examples on coin.

i18n.hi: दूसरी तरफ, ए.के. सिंह बताते हैं, कुछ फनमों पर अंकों को जगह-जगह बैठाया गया है – दशमलव स्थान मान का साफ इस्तेमाल, सिक्कों पर हिंदू उदाहरणों में सबसे पुराने सबूतों में से एक।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Mint Master demonstrating decimal positions to junior scribes on a wax tablet
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master draws columns on a wax tablet, placing numeral marks as younger scribes and coin cutters watch, the tablet beside a small pile of fanams marked with different values.

dialogue.text: Place value was not new in Indian mathematics, but here it stamped itself onto money. A tiny shift in numeral position changed how many fanams paid a soldier or a stone carver.

i18n.hi: भारतीय गणित में स्थान मान पुराना था, पर यहाँ वह सीधे पैसे पर मुहर बन गया। अंक की छोटी सी जगह बदलते ही यह तय होता कि कितने फनम किसी सिपाही या पत्थर तराशने वाले को मिलेंगे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a ledger where Anka regnal years are being written beside temple expenses
panels.action: In a quiet office, Eastern Ganga Mint Master sits cross-legged writing a list of offerings and wages for a temple, each line headed by an Anka regnal year notation, while a drawing of Jagannath shrine lies nearby.

dialogue.text: Time itself was counted in a distinct way. The Anka system of regnal years marked grants and expenses. Its exact formula is complex, yet its line runs down into later Odia practice.

i18n.hi: समय भी अलग अंदाज़ से गिना जाता था। अंक वर्ष नाम की राजावधि प्रणाली से दान और खर्च दर्ज होते। इसका नियम उलझा हुआ है, पर इसकी रेखा आगे की उड़िया परंपरा तक चलती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes and priests discussing Anka dates and rituals in a temple office
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master sits with a temple priest over a palm-leaf calendar, pointing at Anka year markings as the priest gestures toward a model of Jagannath’s chariot festival.

dialogue.text: Under the Puri Gajapati title, Anka dating survived, woven into calendars and rituals. Numbers shaped when festivals fell and how long a king’s favour would be remembered.

i18n.hi: पुरी गजपति नाम के तहत अंक डेटिंग बची रही, कैलेंडर और अनुष्ठानों में बुनी हुई। संख्याएँ तय करतीं कि त्योहार कब पड़ेंगे और राजा की कृपा कितने समय तक याद रहेगी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Konark Sun Temple under construction with overseers tallying workers and payments
panels.action: On the Konark coast, scaffolds climb the rising Sun Temple; Eastern Ganga Mint Master stands with overseers, checking a tally of workers and fanam bundles while stone blocks are hauled into place.

dialogue.text: Behind monuments like the Sun Temple was a quiet arithmetic. Days of labour, stone loads, and fanams in pay were all tracked, so the sacred chariot of Surya could slowly rise from the sand.

i18n.hi: सूर्य मंदिर जैसे स्मारकों के पीछे एक चुप गणित था। मज़दूरी के दिन, पत्थर के बोझ, और फनम में मज़दूरी – सब गिने जाते, ताकि सूर्य का रथ रेत से धीरे-धीरे उठ सके।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of grain fields, tax collectors and a distant royal city linked by faint numeral overlays
panels.action: From above, lush fields with farmers, tax collectors weighing grain, and the distant skyline of Cuttack appear, faint outlines of numerals overlaying the scene as Eastern Ganga Mint Master’s small figure stands in a watchtower.

dialogue.text: Grain from a vishaya village, dues of a mandala, gifts to a mahamandala lord—all these moved because scribes counted, coins carried value, and dates fixed obligations in time.

i18n.hi: किसी विशय गाँव का अनाज, मंडल की लगान, महामंडल के स्वामी को भेंट – ये सब चलते थे क्योंकि लिखे पढ़े लोग गिनती करते थे, सिक्के कीमत ढोते थे और तारीखें वादों को समय में बाँधती थीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Mint Master’s thoughtful face as he handles an old copper plate and a freshly struck coin together
panels.action: Eastern Ganga Mint Master sits alone at dusk, holding an aged copper plate in one hand and a newly struck fanam in the other, his eyes reflecting both the engraved letters and the sharp numerals.

dialogue.speaker: Eastern Ganga Mint Master
dialogue.text: Without the right number in the right place, even a lion on gold is only metal.

i18n.hi: अगर अंक सही जगह पर न बैठे, तो सोने पर बना सिंह भी सिर्फ धातु रह जाता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of archive shelves of plates and manuscripts fading into the silhouette of temples and forts
panels.action: Rows of shelves stacked with copper plates, palm-leaf manuscripts and small coin jars stretch into the distance; as the view recedes, these merge visually into outlines of temples, forts and cities on the horizon, with Eastern Ganga Mint Master a small figure walking among them.

dialogue.text: In the Eastern Ganga age, ledgers, Anka years and decimal fanams were the unseen frame of power—showing how, in any kingdom, the quiet line of numbers can be as decisive as the sword.

i18n.hi: पूर्वी गंगा युग में बहियाँ, अंक वर्ष और दशमलवी फनम शक्ति की अदृश्य ढाँचा थे – दिखाते हुए कि किसी भी राज्य में संख्याओं की शांत रेखा तलवार जितनी निर्णायक हो सकती है।

title_i18n.en: The Panji and the Decimal Coin

subtitle_i18n.en: Ledgers of the Lion: How Numbers Held Up the Eastern Ganga Realm
subtitle_i18n.hi: सिंह की बहीखाता: कैसे संख्याएँ संभाले रखती थीं पूर्वी गंगा राज्य
